```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)

library(MASS)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(GGally)
library(DataExplorer)
library(patchwork)
library(corrplot)
library(factoextra)
library(reshape2)
library(scales)
```
# Load Boston dataset

```{r load}
data("Boston")
boston <- Boston

# Quick data check
dim(boston)
names(boston)
head(boston)
summary(boston)


# Missing values
plot_intro(boston)
plot_missing(boston)
```


# Variable explanation
```{r var}
var_info <- data.frame(
Variable = names(boston),
Description = c(
"Per capita crime rate by town",
"Proportion of residential land zoned for lots > 25,000 sq.ft.",
"Proportion of non-retail business acres per town",
"Charles River dummy variable (1 if tract bounds river; 0 otherwise)",
"Nitric oxides concentration (parts per 10 million)",
"Average number of rooms per dwelling",
"Proportion of owner-occupied units built prior to 1940",
"Weighted distances to five Boston employment centres",
"Index of accessibility to radial highways",
"Full-value property-tax rate per $10,000",
"Pupil-teacher ratio by town",
"Proportion of population that is lower status",
"Median value of owner-occupied homes ($1000s)",
"Derived: Tax per room (tax / average rooms)"
)
)
var_info
```

# Correlation matrix
```{r corr}
num <- boston[, sapply(boston, is.numeric)]
M <- cor(num)
corrplot(M, method = "pie")
round(M, 2)
```

# Pairwise scatter matrix 
Charles River dummy variable:

- 1 if the tract bounds the Charles River

- 0 otherwise
```{r scat}
ggpairs(
  boston,
  columns = c("crim", "rm", "age", "dis", "rad", "tax", "medv"),
  mapping = aes(color = factor(chas)),  # categorical coloring
  lower = list(continuous = wrap("smooth", alpha = 0.3, size = 0.4)),
  upper = list(continuous = wrap("cor", size = 3)),
  diag = list(continuous = wrap("densityDiag", alpha = 0.5))
)
```

# Feature engineering: tax per room
```{r feature}
boston <- boston %>%
mutate(tax_per_room = tax / rm)
summary(boston$tax_per_room)

# Scale numeric features

scaled_data <- as.data.frame(scale(boston[, sapply(boston, is.numeric)]))
head(scaled_data)
```
